newsitem.title: PERU: Telefonica rejects ruling on cellphones.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica rejects ruling on cellphones.

text.p: Spanish-controlled Telefonica del Peru rejected Monday a ruling from Peru's telecommunications regulatory body OSIPTEL that it share its nationwide cellular roaming facilities with U.S.-owned competitor Tele 2000.

Telefonica said in a statement that OSIPTEL's ruling, if carried out, would represent a "de facto expropriation" of its facilities by Tele 2000, which would paralyze a $160 million future investment plan and "create a climate of legal insecurity in the telecommunications sector."
OSIPTEL officials said Telefnica had 15 days from the July 1 ruling to comply or face a financial penalty.

Tele 2000 announced in a statement Monday that "as a consequence (of the OSIPTEL decision), clients will soon be able to receive and make calls directly and automatically from any place in Peru where cellular service exists."

Telefnica is owned by Telefnica de Espaa, while BellSouth Corp controls Tele 2000. Telefnica, which has a monopoly on regular telephone services until 1999, currently offers nationwide cellular services, while Tele 2000 is limited to Lima and its neighboring port Callao.

"Roaming is universally understood as a technical and operative facility which is shared reciprocally between mobile cellular telephone operators under agreements of mutual convenience," Telefnica said. "Nowhere in the world are operating companies obliged to give away the roaming service."

Sharing its nationwide roaming service with Tele 2000 would require additional network servicing costs, deny the state the $50 million to $100 million it could charge for provincial concessions, and "influence the planning of future investments of Telefnica del Per," the statement added.

Telefnica said it had already invested $80 million in its provincial cellular network, "and we were projecting an additional investment of $160 million, which, if the ruling is upheld, will be paralyzed immediately."
